title: Growable Data
goal: Vec for lists, HashMap for lookups, and the entry idiom for counting.

sections.text: `Vec<T>` is Rust's growable list. Build it with the `vec!` macro or start empty with `Vec::new()`. Growth is mutation, so a vec you push into must be bound with `let mut`.

sections.caption: vec! builds, push grows, mut permits.

sections.text: A plain array `[10, 20, 30]` has a fixed size baked into its type and no `push`. Arrays and vecs look alike at a glance; their types and their errors are different.

Walk a vec with `for n in &v`. Borrowing the vec in the loop lets you use it again afterward - the ampersand will make full sense in the Core decks; for now it is simply how you loop without giving the vec away.

The counting idiom deserves memorizing: `map.entry(key).or_insert(0)` returns a mutable reference to the entry, creating it with 0 first if needed. Bump through the reference with `*count += 1`. The star matters - you are changing the value the reference points at, and the last puzzle makes you feel exactly that.

explanation: Vec for lists, HashMap for lookups, and the entry idiom for counting.
